role_in_parent: Supplies the explicitly required boundary case p = 5, which earlier failed decompositions omitted after restricting other lemmas to larger N.
statement_nl: Let p = 5. For each k in {1,2,3,4}, let I(k) be the unique integer in {1,2,3,4} such that k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod 5), and let S = { k in {1,2,3} : I(k+1) < I(k) }. Then |S| >= floor(5/4).

domain_restrictions: p is the integer 5 (no universal quantification over p)
indices k used to define I range over {1,2,3,4}
when forming S, k is restricted to {1,2,3}
I(k) is required to be an integer representative in the set {1,2,3,4}
congruence k * I(k) ≡ 1 is taken modulo p = 5
the comparison I(k+1) < I(k) is the usual total order on integers
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: With p = 5 and I: {1,2,3,4} -> {1,2,3,4} defined by I(k) ≡ k^{-1} (mod 5) as the unique representative in {1,2,3,4}, let S = { k ∈ {1,2,3} : I(k+1) < I(k) }. Then |S| ≥ 1 (since floor(5/4) = 1).
quantifier_order: p is assigned the constant value 5
for each k ∈ {1,2,3,4} there exists a unique I(k) ∈ {1,2,3,4} such that k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod 5)

variables.name: p
variables.role: fixed modulus; p is assigned the value 5

variables.name: k
variables.role: index variable used to define I(k); when defining S the same symbol k is restricted to {1,2,3}

variables.name: I
variables.role: I(k) is the (unique) multiplicative inverse of k modulo p, represented as the representative in {1,2,3,4}

variables.name: S
variables.role: S = { k in {1,2,3} : I(k+1) < I(k) }, counts adjacent descents of the sequence I(1),I(2),I(3),I(4) for indices 1..3

witness_dependencies: I(k) is an existential witness depending on k (and on the fixed p = 5); there is one witness for each k in {1,2,3,4}
uniqueness of I(k) is asserted within the codomain {1,2,3,4}
membership of k in S depends on the pair of witnesses I(k) and I(k+1)
the set S is completely determined by the family of witnesses {I(1),I(2),I(3),I(4)}
